title: A Movie Credit You Almost Never See
summary:
Suzanne Collins is the writer behind the "Hunger Games" books. Without her, none of the movies would exist.

That is very true for the newest movie, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." It was the top movie at the box office on its first weekend. If you stay to watch the credits, you will see some words that almost never appear in movies: "Adaptation by Suzanne Collins."

Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie wrote the movie's screenplay, which is the written words of the movie. Collins got credit for turning her 2024 book of the same name into a movie. That is very rare in Hollywood.

The Writers Guild of America is the group for people who write movies. Its book of rules says the group does not like the "Adaptation by" credit being used a lot. But it can be used in special cases, when a writer helps shape how the story is built for the screen, even if they did not write the screenplay. It can only be used after a formal process called arbitration.
why_it_matters: It shows why the names at the end of a movie matter, because they tell you who really made the story.
